findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r3): the wrong-person awaiting UPDATE as executed still lacks the taken_over_at backstop — the dedicated guarded SQL ships unwired (dead code), and the race pin is vacuous (it drives the dead SQL, not the POST route)
findings.evidence: apply_wrong_person False arm: 'case sql.update_reference_call_status(config.db, id_uuid, sql.AwaitingCorrection, "", "contact_invalid", sql.ContactInitiated)' — update_reference_call_status.sql: 'WHERE id = $1 AND status = $5::reference_call_status' (NO taken_over_at clause). mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person.sql exists with 'AND taken_over_at IS NULL' but grep shows its only references are sql.gleam (the generated module) — zero callers in form_handler/webhooks/trigger. The test at 1729-1765 calls 'rc_sql.mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person(db, call)' DIRECTLY (plus do_take_over for setup) — it never drives handle_wrong_person_post / apply_wrong_person; removing the backstop from the executed path (or unwiring the SQL entirely, as shipped) leaves it green. The guarded SQL also lacks the correction_cycles = 0 backstop its sibling mark_awaiting_correction gained (r3 N21).
findings.detail: The r3 blocker's fix was authored but never wired: the handler still executes the unguarded UPDATE, so a take-over committing between the token read and the UPDATE still yanks a landlord-handled row into awaiting_correction (take-over never changes status) and dead-ends it permanently — the exact r2/r3 consequence. The race test pins a dead function, not the POST path.
findings.recommended_fix: Wire mark_awaiting_correction_wrong_person into apply_wrong_person's False arm (delete the update_reference_call_status call), add AND correction_cycles = 0 to the SQL, and replace the direct-SQL test with a POST-route race test (neutralize backstop -> red).

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r3 W3 partial): the co-nudge exclusion is forward-only — legacy untagged co-nudge entries in append-only attempts logs still match the delivery-failure find, so a bounce of the APPLICANT's address on a pre-deploy corrected row still exhausts it and fabricates referee_contact_invalid
findings.location: server/src/reference_checks/sql/find_reference_call_by_send_ref.sql:82-98 (EXISTS arm); server/src/reference_checks/sweep.gleam:812-822 (co_nudge_entry — tag written only from this deploy)
findings.evidence: EXISTS arm: 'WHERE e->>'detail' = $3 AND e->>'outcome' = 'delivered' AND NOT (e ? 'kind')' — the exclusion filters on a 'kind' KEY; entries appended before this deploy have no such key. co_nudge_entry: '#("kind", json.string("co_nudge"))' — only new writes carry it. attempts is append-only; no migration retro-tags existing co-nudge entries.
findings.detail: Rows whose co-nudge entries were appended pre-deploy keep matching: a redelivered bounce of the applicant's address on a corrected row reads send_is_post_correction = true and exhausts to unreachable + referee_contact_invalid — the fraud signal fabricated on a referee whose contact never failed.
findings.recommended_fix: Retro-tag existing co-nudge entries in a migration (or exclude by detail-prefix convention), or scope the find's kind-aware containment to entries written after the deploy marker.

findings.title: The r3 W3 pin is vacuous: co_nudge_bounce_stands_down_test's fixture timestamps stand down via the typed stale-bounce gate alone — removing the kind exclusion would NOT turn the test red; the producer-side kind tag is also unpinned
findings.evidence: Fixture: co-nudge entry '{"at":"2026-08-01T09:00:00Z",...,"detail":"co_nudge_send_1","kind":"co_nudge"}' — corrected_at = now() (2026-08-13). A co-nudge send is by definition POST-correction; with the entry's 'at' pre-correction, send_is_post_correction = false and the handler's 'matched_send_at == "" || send_is_post_correction' gate stands down even if the kind exclusion were deleted. No sweep-level test asserts co_nudge_entry writes the kind tag (grep of sweep_test.gleam: zero hits).
findings.detail: A guard against fabricated fraud signals must be pinned by a test that bites. The only W3 pin cannot detect a regression of the exclusion or of the tag write — both would pass CI.
findings.recommended_fix: Rebuild the fixture with a post-correction co-nudge timestamp (now() + interval, like the control arm) so only the kind exclusion stands it down; add a sweep unit test asserting the co-nudge entry carries kind=co_nudge.

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r3 N5): the edit-open path still unconditionally overwrites another row's in-progress typed trio — choosing Correct/Substitute on a second row discards the first row's values (the success-clear half is fixed; the choice half is not)
findings.evidence: RefcheckSubstitute -> '#(Model(..menu_closed, refcheck_edit: Some(prefill_refcheck_edit(model, call_id, RefcheckEditSubstitute))), effect.none())' — no check whether model.refcheck_edit already targets a DIFFERENT call_id; contrast the Ok arm's 'let edit_kept = case model.refcheck_edit { Some(edit) if edit.call_id == call_id -> None; other -> other }' (r3 N2 scoping, success-side only).

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r3 N14): Escape-to-close remains wired to the menu div, which never receives focus after clicking ⋯ — the natural click-then-Escape flow does nothing

findings.title: STILL PRESENT (r3 N20, carried-with-reason but leaves a hole): trio_matches_row now uses the SNAPSHOT basis for all three fields — a corrected successor re-submitted with its ORIGINAL trio returns 200 no-op and silently drops the typed referee (who is no longer the successor's effective contact)
findings.evidence: trio_matches_row: 'trio.name == row.contact_name && trio.email == option.unwrap(row.contact_email, "") && trio.phone == option.unwrap(row.contact_phone, "")' — the successor's snapshot. If the successor was later corrected (corrected_name/email set to a different person), a re-submit of the ORIGINAL trio matches the snapshot -> 'existing' -> 200, typed trio discarded.
findings.detail: The r3 N20 recommendation was the effective-name basis; the fixer chose snapshot with a rationale, but that leaves the r2 W7-class silent drop in the corrected-successor edge: the landlord types a referee and the system returns a row for someone else.
findings.recommended_fix: Compare against the effective trio (corrected ?? snapshot) like trio_matches, so a re-submit that no longer matches the row's real contact 409s.

findings.title: Malformed 'at' handling is inconsistent and unguarded in practice: an 'at'-less delivered entry exhausts a corrected row via the matched_send_at=='' short-circuit (bypassing the regex stand-down), while a prefix-shaped malformed 'at' passes the prefix-anchored regex and raises, dropping the whole webhook event; the malformed branch has no test
findings.evidence: webhooks: 'case row.matched_send_at == "" || row.send_is_post_correction { True -> exhaust_row(...) }' — matched_send_at is COALESCE((SELECT e->>'at' ...), '') so a delivered entry WITHOUT 'at' yields '' -> exhaust. SQL: 'CASE WHEN e->>'at' ~ '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}[T ][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}' THEN (e->>'at')::timestamptz >= rc.corrected_at ELSE false END' — the regex is start-anchored only; '2026-08-01T08:00:00junk' passes and ::timestamptz raises (whole find fails -> event dropped). No test exercises the regex branch.
findings.detail: The r3 N14sql fix guards only fully-malformed strings; the '' short-circuit and the prefix-parse cases disagree — one exhausts a corrected row on malformed data, the other raises. Both are defense-in-depth failures with no pin.
findings.recommended_fix: Anchor the regex to the full string, and treat '' matched_send_at as stand-down for corrected rows (fallback is pre-correction-only now). Add a malformed-'at' fixture test.

findings.title: A genuine post-correction delivery failure on the fallback leg can no longer match the find — the blanket fallback-disable (the accepted r3 W2 fix) means a crash-mid-tick post-correction send whose send_ref was never appended leaves the row cycling until the sweep's sequence terminal, without the referee_contact_invalid stamp
findings.evidence: 'OR (rc.correction_cycles = 0 AND $1 <> '' AND CASE ... END = $1)' — post-correction, only the send-ref EXISTS arm can match; a genuine post-correction bounce whose attempts append crashed (the fallback's original reason to exist) matches nothing -> no exhaustion, no stamp, no audit.
findings.detail: The W2 trade-off's residual: the webhook exhaustion leg now misses the crash-mid-tick failure case entirely (the sweep terminal eventually closes the row, but via sequence_exhausted, not the contact-invalid stamp). Documented-accepted, but the fraud signal is lost for a real failure.
findings.recommended_fix: Carry a corrected_at comparison into the fallback (accept envelopes that postdate corrected_at on unchanged channels) instead of a blanket disable.

findings.title: run_action_with_prechecks: a DB Error from verify_vacancy_active falls into the catch-all '_ -> action()' — a transient error on the archived check lets an action run on an archived vacancy
findings.evidence: 'case app_sql.verify_vacancy_active(db, vacancy_uuid, landlord_uuid) { Ok(pog.Returned(_, [vacancy_row])) if vacancy_row.is_archived -> ...422... _ -> action() }' — the _ arm folds Error(_) (DB failure) and 0-row together with 'not archived'.
findings.detail: The sibling precheck (verify_application_in_vacancy) treats Error as 404; this one treats Error as proceed. Fail-open on a guard.
findings.recommended_fix: Split the _ arm: Error -> 500 json_error (brand copy); Ok 0-row/not-archived -> action().

findings.title: webhooks exhaust_row's '_' arm swallows a DB Error on the exhaustion UPDATE — the exact class r3 N13 fixed in form_handler's exhaust_wrong_person remains in the webhook leg
findings.evidence: 'Ok(pog.Returned(_, [_, ..])) -> { ...stamp/audit/notify... } _ -> // 0 rows: ... stand down Nil' — Error(err) is folded into the stand-down arm with no log, no Sentry capture (contrast exhaust_wrong_person's r3 N8 split: Error -> wisp.log_error + sentry_client.capture).
findings.detail: A DB failure on the webhook exhaustion UPDATE silently drops the event — the row stays live, the fraud stamp + audit + notification never fire, and nothing is observable.
findings.recommended_fix: Split the _ arm: 0-row -> Nil (legit stand-down); Error -> sentry capture 'ReferenceWebhookExhaustFailed' + log.
